description: A DAG built to demonstrate the per-step profiling tools: `sweep` (parallel-speedup study), `run --selected` (run selected steps and their dependencies), `run --profile` (per-step table), and the default auto-logging profile store. The `build.app` step is a small CPU-bound workload that ACTUALLY scales with its inner parallelism: it splits a fixed amount of pure-shell work across N parallel workers, where N is the inner-jobs width the runner passes in via the step's jobs_flag. So `sweep --step build.app --jobs 1..8` shows a real speedup curve, and every run/sweep auto-appends resource-usage CSVs to ./.dagrun/profiles/.

steps.desc: parallel compile (simulated CPU work that scales with -j)
steps.description: A stand-in for a parallel build. It reads the inner-jobs width the runner appends to the command (via jobs_flag '-j%d', so -j4 arrives as $1), splits ~1.2M pure-shell iterations across that many background workers, and waits for them. More workers finish the fixed work sooner (up to the core count), so `sweep --step build.app --jobs 1..N` produces a genuine speedup curve. Sweep this step to see it.
steps.cmd: run() { n=${1#-j}; n=${n:-1}; per=$((1200000 / n)); pids=; for i in $(seq 1 "$n"); do ( x=0; while [ "$x" -lt "$per" ]; do x=$((x+1)); done ) & pids="$pids $!"; done; wait $pids; echo "built (split 1200000 iters across ${n} worker(s))"; }; run

steps.description: A quick downstream step so the DAG is more than one node: it depends on build.app and just echoes. Use `run --selected test.unit` to run it after build.app, or add `--ignore-selected-deps` when the build output is already present and only this step should run.
